title: Part 2: How Many Dominoes to Topple a 1 KM Tower? 🤔
description:
How many dominoes does it take to topple a 1 km tower? Comment your number before the first one lands!

Part 2 of Domino Giant. The first domino is 5 cm tall, and every next domino is 1.65 times bigger in every dimension. That is the biggest jump this model can manage: at 1.7 times, the first domino bounces off the second and the chain stalls. Each domino stands half a domino-height away from the one that will hit it. One flick starts the line: each domino tips over its lower edge, falls under gravity and pushes the next, bigger one. The line ends at a 1 km tower, and the first domino that is taller than the tower knocks it over. The counter shows how many dominoes have toppled so far, the dashed line marks the height of the tower, and everyday objects show the scale as the camera pulls back. Big dominoes fall much more slowly than small ones, so the playback speed changes along the way and is always shown on screen.
This is a simplified rigid-block model: every domino is a solid block that pivots on its edge, contact is frictionless and does not bounce, and the tower is treated as a lighter block. Physics, picture and sound are generated by code (seed 90), with no footage, samples or stock media.
What number did you guess?
#simulation #satisfying #dominoes
